chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Riʾāb narrated from Abū ʿUbaydah, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

Indeed, when a slave absconds from his masters and then steals, his hand is not cut off while he is a fugitive, because he is in the position of an apostate from Islam. Rather, he is called to return to his masters and to enter into Islam. Then if he refuses to return to his masters, his hand is cut off for the theft, then he is killed. And the apostate, if he steals, is in the same position.

key_terms.أَبَقَ: absconded or fled from his masters
key_terms.الْمُرْتَدِّ: the apostate, one who has turned away from Islam

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a fugitive slave or apostate who commits theft in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning an absconding slave who commits theft, treating his fugitive state as analogous to riddah in legal consequence. It states that he is first called back to obedience and Islam, and if he refuses, the punishment for theft is carried out and then capital punishment follows; the same ruling is said to apply to the apostate who steals.
